fit: single Parkinson case after a seven-ingredient Kampo extract
assessment: The authors describe daytime visual hallucinations and dream enactment ceasing two days after treatment began. The six-month statement addresses parasomnia only. The oral extract included jujube, cinnamon bark and ginger among seven ingredients, without figs. The uncontrolled timeline supplies no attribution to a constituent or dried fig effect.

fit: patient, caregiver and clinician measures and future dementia
assessment: The baseline Parkinson cohort included 328 participants. Of 202 followed without baseline dementia, 51 developed dementia. The instruments observe neuropsychiatric symptoms, and the study analyzes future dementia rather than post-ingestion visual episode frequency.

fit: sensed presence phenotype in Lewy body dementia
assessment: Ten participants reported feeling a presence and 24 did not. The original distinguishes sensed presence without sight or sound from visual episodes. The comparison looks at imaging and symptoms without a culinary exposure.

fit: visual attention task across dementia groups
assessment: The study compares visual attention and modeled sensory evidence in a reused Lewy body cohort, including 13 people with Parkinson dementia. Task performance is distinct from hallucination frequency following fig ingestion.

fit: underrecruited placebo comparison for minor Parkinson visual hallucinations
assessment: The CHEVAL trial randomized 91 participants, 46 to rivastigmine and 45 to placebo. It ended recruitment early. The reported time-to-treated-psychosis and dementia comparisons were inconclusive. Treatment initiation is distinct from visual episodes per time unit and is unrelated to a dried fig exposure.

fit: severe postoperative deficiency and route-dependent magnesium response
assessment: The two surgical cases involve losses, seizures and confusion. Orange juice carried oral magnesium sulfate in one case, while oral salts failed during recurrence in the other before parenteral replacement helped. No visual hallucination frequency or Parkinson diagnosis was documented.

fit: cross-sectional retinal measurements by visual symptom group
assessment: Ocular imaging compares 26 people with illusions, 28 with hallucinations and 28 with neither. Parafoveal thinning was associated with the hallucination group. The comparison measures symptom presence and retina structure, without food timing. The nested manuscript and follow-up reuse this cohort.

fit: telephone follow-up of the baseline ocular cohort
assessment: The two-year interviews reclassified visual symptom states and checked concurrent eye and medication treatment. The same cohort and transition results appear in conference member 1436. The original abstract gives presence categories rather than counted episodes after fig consumption.

fit: frequency and duration in a nested Parkinson visual symptom comparison
assessment: The accepted manuscript compares 54 people from the parent 82-person cohort. Hallucinations were reported more often and lasted longer than illusions on the Psycho-Sensory Hallucinations Scale, p = 0.02 for each. The analysis separates symptom groups and supplies no ingestion-timed exposure comparison.
